layers.title: Terrain height
layers.processing: Height tiles for zoom 9 to 15, to the nearest 0.1 m: this 1 m terrain inside the 3 km box, and round it, out to a 10 km square, JEZ_ctx_B_soc_008_DTM_MOLAtopography_DeltaGeoid_20m_Eqc_latTs0_lon0 (20 m, NASA/JPL-Caltech/MSSS/USGS (Fergason, Galuszka and Hare 2020)). Over the last 1.5 km of the square the heights are eased to the box's lowest point, because the map has no terrain beyond it; that easing is for the picture only and is not data. Routes and slopes use only the 1 m terrain.

layers.instrument: Thermal Emission Imaging System (THEMIS), night infrared
layers.productId: nili_THEMIS_NightIR_Controlled_oct2018 (USGS THEMIS controlled mosaic, October 2018, as shipped in SIM 3464)
layers.acquiredFrom: 2002 at the earliest (THEMIS began mapping in 2002; not stated in the file)
layers.acquiredTo: Before October 2018, the mosaic version named in its folder
layers.realDetail: About 100 m: 30 pixels across the 3 km site box
caveats: Brightness stretched to 8 bits for display, not a temperature.
Far coarser than the walking map: one pixel is 100 m. A guide to where footing changes, not a footing map.
Dust cover hides what is underneath; a dusty rock surface can look like loose ground.
layers.credit: NASA/JPL-Caltech/Arizona State University; mosaic by USGS; in Sun and Stack 2020 (USGS SIM 3464)
layers.title: Night-time warmth
layers.processing: Read from nili_THEMIS_NightIR_Controlled_oct2018.tif over a 12 km square centred on the site marker (local copy in data/raw, warped from its own projection onto the app's grid), coloured along a ramp from value 40 to 200, and cut into tiles for zoom 9 to 12. The map stretches them at closer zooms.

legend.note: Relative brightness of the night infrared mosaic, not a temperature. Warmer at night often means rock or firm ground; cooler means fine, loose material.

Checked against the tilt the rover measured at 116 stops: typical difference 1.4 degrees, 9 in 10 within 4.0 degrees. Rover drivers choose gentle ground, so steep slopes are less well checked.
A short steep step, such as a ledge under about 3 m, can be missed.
layers.title: Slope
layers.processing: Steepest slope at each 1 m cell of the terrain, then the steepest of those in each routing cell. Cells are narrower east to west at this latitude and the spacing is corrected for it.
